description:
FILED s451y (Opus, round 10 agent Y) from the #612 probes.  PRE-EXISTING on
main 718db6b and unrelated to #612 -- the paren is a red herring, the
non-paren spelling fails identically.

REPRO (perl vs ./runpcl):
    use v5.24; my %hh;
    @{ $hh{k} }[0,1] = (11,12);
    print join(",", @{$hh{k}}), " ref=", ref($hh{k}), "\n";
        perl: 11,12 ref=ARRAY
        PCL:  (empty) ref=ARRAY        <-- SILENT WRONG

    use v5.24; my %h;
    @{ $h{k} }{qw(x y)} = (1,2);
    print join(",", map {"$_=$h{k}{$_}"} sort keys %{$h{k}}), "\n";
        perl: x=1,y=2
        PCL:  DIES

THE DISCRIMINATOR (measured, both directions):
    @{ $r }[0,1] = (11,12);        my $r = [];   WORKS
    @{ ($r) }[0,1] = (11,12);      my $r = [];   WORKS
    ($r)->@[0,1] = (11,12);        my $r = [];   WORKS
    @{ ($hr) }{qw(x y)} = (1,2);   my $hr = {};  WORKS
    @{ $hh{k} }[0,1] = (11,12);    %hh empty     WRONG (array made, empty)
    @{ ($hh{k}) }[0,1] = (11,12);  %hh empty     WRONG (identically)
    @{ (0,$hh{k}) }{qw(x y)} = ..  %hh empty     DIES

So it is not the paren and not the postfix spelling: it is an lvalue SLICE
whose container has to be AUTOVIVIFIED from an undef hash/array ELEMENT.  The
autovivification itself happens (ref($hh{k}) is ARRAY afterwards), so the
element is being vivified into a DIFFERENT box from the one p-aslice then
writes through -- the ELEMENT spelling `@{ $hh{k} } = (7,8)` (no subscript)
is right, and so is every case whose container is already a ref.

WHERE TO LOOK: `Pl::ExprToCL::gen_array_slice_form` /
`gen_hash_slice_form` -> `_slice_container_form`, which wraps a non-bare
container in `p-cast-@` / `p-cast-%`.  In an ASSIGNMENT the slice is the LHS,
so the container is lowered in lvalue context and `p-cast-@` autovivifies --
the question is whether the vivified aggregate is stored back into the
element's box or into a copy.  Compare with the working element sibling
(`p-array-deref-=` on `@{ $hh{k} }`), which is the same autovivification one
node up.

BAR: the seven rows above vs perl, both directions; the hash spelling must
stop DYING; corpus-diff + emission-ab (an lvalue-slice emission change).
subject: an lvalue SLICE through an AUTOVIVIFIED hash/array element writes nowhere: `@{ $h{k} }[0,1] = (11,12)` leaves the array EMPTY (hash spelling DIES)
